verdict.rationale: Checkout.com documents first-class idempotency via the `Cko-Idempotency-Key` header. It covers every money-moving endpoint (/payments, authorizations, captures, refunds, voids, cancellations, payment-contexts, transfers), keys are cached on 2xx responses, and the idempotency window is configurable. The docs explicitly frame this as safe retries after network errors or timeouts, which covers the core no-duplicate-charges goal. missing for 10: idempotency covers only a listed subset of endpoints rather than 'any API request', no independent or hands-on corroboration of retry behavior.
